clue.text: Sack Sir Henry for starting a blaze

parts.note: to sack someone is to dismiss them, to fire them
Sir Henry Wood was the conductor who founded the Proms concerts

explanation.surface: An order to dismiss a knight named Henry because he lit a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood founded London's Proms concerts; the surface makes 'Sack' a dismissal of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Logs and sticks burned as fuel are what you gather to light a fire.

clue.text: Poem written up on course — not quite a failure

indicators.note: written up in a down clue means the poem's letters run upward, backwards

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: not quite means the racecourse loses its final letter

parts.note: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A poem about a racecourse that doesn't quite succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'If' turned up gives FI; Ascot is an English racecourse, cut to ASCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating flop, a complete failure.

clue.text: Loop the loops again, and get a kick out of it

definitions.meaning: to coil a rope once more

definitions.text: get a kick out of it
definitions.meaning: to spring back, as a gun does when fired

explanation.surface: Doing aerobatics a second time and enjoying the thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get a kick out of it' sounds like enjoyment but means a gun's backward kick.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind into coils once more, and the backward jerk a firearm gives on firing.

clue.text: Protest about tar found during visiting dignitary's stroll

indicators.note: about means the protest's letters go round the sailor's

parts.note: a walkout is a strike or protest by leaving
AB, able seaman, is a sailor, as is a tar

explanation.surface: A demonstration breaks out when a sailor appears during a royal walk among crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found during' is link; a walkabout is a royal's informal stroll among a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Royals and other dignitaries make informal tours on foot among the public.

clue.text: A foolish tradition, but constituents in Wales loved it

indicators.note: constituents means the letters of the following words are the components, reassembled

explanation.surface: A silly old custom that the Welsh adored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters in Wales, but signals rearranging WALES LOVED IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstition or folk belief handed down and held foolishly is called by this phrase.

clue.text: These states give backing to party movement

indicators.note: backing means the word for the party is turned round to run the other way

parts.note: Lab is short for the UK Labour Party
a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: Some countries lend their support to a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like political support, but it turns LAB into BAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are known collectively by the name of the sea they border.

clue.text: Indistinguishable from a Liberal president

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Hard to tell apart from a liberal head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ike was Dwight Eisenhower, US President in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are identical or very similar cannot be told apart.

clue.text: Unusually great man singled out for attack

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of great are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A remarkably great man was picked out to be assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' turns GREAT into TARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimed at, chosen as the object of an assault.

clue.text: It's wrong in court persistently to punish

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for courting

parts.note: to chase is to pursue romantically, courting persistently

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of it's are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: It's unjust to keep penalising someone in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but means to woo; 'wrong' rearranges IT'S to TIS, and 'in' places it within the courting word.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate or discipline severely is a synonym for punishing.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of merit in a brace of musicians?

definitions.meaning: an honour or award given in praise
in music, the bracket joining the staves of a score is also called by this name

explanation.surface: Two musicians receive a prize together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' looks like a pair of players; it is the printed bracket linking staves in a score.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour bestowed for achievement, and the musical term for the bracket that ties staves together.

clue.text: Start of sedition by republicans, capturing king in mountains

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of sedition is taken
capturing means the republicans' letters hold the king's letters within them

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Rebels launch a revolt in the hills and seize the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'republicans' suggests US politics but means the Irish Republican Army; 'capturing' gives IERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged range of peaks, especially in Spain or Latin America.

clue.text: Highly exciting lawsuit ending in sound agreement

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit; 'ending in' just places it before the next piece

indicators.note: sound means the agreement's word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: A thrilling court case finishes with a reliable settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' seems to mean reliable but signals a homophone: PACT said aloud gives PACKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or book full of thrilling incidents is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Mate in the People's Republic

definitions.meaning: in cockney rhyming slang, '... plate' rhymes with mate, so a pal
the state in East Asia officially called the People's Republic

explanation.surface: A friend living in a Communist state.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang shortens 'china plate' (mate) to its first word, so 'my old china' is 'my friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a friend, and the name of the vast Asian country governed from Beijing.

clue.text: Popular Bishop of Rome, albeit severe

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the Pope is Bishop of Rome, and several popes took the name Clement

explanation.surface: A well-liked pope who was nonetheless stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'albeit' only joins the definition; Clement was the name of fourteen popes.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh or stormy, as of weather, is a sense shared with severe.

clue.text: New sieves chosen for sticking together

indicators.note: new here means the letters of the following words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Freshly picked sieves are selected for gluing.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of staying united or adhering firmly is a noun for sticking together.

clue.text: Instruct a number out east, including new student

indicators.note: including means the shortened number holds the new student's letters inside it
out means the east letter is removed from the number

parts.note: eighteen is a number
E is east
N is new
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: Teach a group to leave the east, taking in a fresh pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: EIGHTEEN with an E out leaves EIGHTEN, and 'including' puts N and L after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone knowledge or understanding is to teach or instruct them.

clue.text: Wrongly estimate the secret service's leader in Israel

parts.note: MI, Military Intelligence, is the British secret service, plus the S of the possessive
in the Old Testament, judges such as Samson and Gideon led Israel

explanation.surface: Miscalculate the head of Mossad, Israel's spy chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical Book of Judges tells of leaders of Israel; 'leader' looks like a spy chief.
explanation.definitionFit: To form a wrong opinion or calculation is to get one's estimate wrong.

clue.text: Crack upset thrifty type during exam once

indicators.note: during means the overturned saver sits inside the old exam

parts.note: CSE, Certificate of Secondary Education, was a British school exam until 1988

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters of the thrifty type are turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: a saver is a thrifty person

explanation.surface: A frugal person breaks down during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SAVER to REVAS; the CSE was a British school-leaving exam, replaced in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep fissure in a glacier is a crack in the ice.

clue.text: Annoyingly like an Irish girl with a prickly sensation

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
tingly describes a prickling, stinging feeling

explanation.surface: A young Irish woman with pins and needles is irksome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like an' is link; IR, RITA and TINGLY run straight together.
explanation.definitionFit: In a vexing, exasperating way is how an irritant behaves.

clue.text: Father's got a girl — a dish

parts.note: pa is father; the 's is 'has' in 'Father's got'
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Dad has a daughter and serves a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's got' means 'father has got', so PA is simply followed by ELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish with seafood or chicken.

clue.text: He pays rent to odd Characters in Leeds — get it?

indicators.note: odd characters in means the first, third and fifth letters of Leeds are taken

parts.note: see? means do you understand

explanation.surface: A tenant pays money to strange people in Leeds, if you follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd Characters' looks like strange people; it takes L, E, S from Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holding a lease is the one paying rent to the landlord.

clue.text: The early efforts of one university in throwing the javelin

indicators.note: throwing suggests the letters of javelin are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A student's first attempts at hurling the javelin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places I and U among the letters of JAVELIN before the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Works produced by an author or artist in youth are called juvenilia.

clue.text: She wept when stony — and no kid!

definitions.text: She wept when stony — and no kid!

parts.words: She wept when stony — and no kid!
parts.note: Greek myth's mother whose many children were slain by gods and who, turned to stone, wept forever

explanation.surface: A woman who cried after hardening, and not joking either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no kid' looks like 'no kidding' but means she was left with no children at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical queen of Thebes, grieving for her slain offspring, was turned to a weeping rock.

clue.text: A cricketer's elegance of movement

definitions.meaning: W. G. ... was the most famous English cricketer of the Victorian era
poise and smoothness in the way one moves

explanation.surface: A batsman's poised style on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: W. G. Grace was a celebrated English cricketer; the clue reads as describing any player's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of a legendary English batsman, and a word for poise and fluency in motion.

clue.text: Extremely desirable situation for an absolute ruler

indicators.note: extremely means only the extreme letters, first and last, of desirable are used

parts.note: a spot is a place or situation

explanation.surface: A dictator would think it the ideal location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as 'very' but takes the first and last letters of 'desirable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant holds unchecked power, the mark of an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Way to carry gear the French used in this game

indicators.note: to carry means the way's letters hold the gear's letters inside them

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
kit is gear or equipment
les is French for 'the' (plural)

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to transport the French team's kit used in a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a British pub game of bowling at wooden pins; 'to carry' puts the gear inside the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A game in which wooden pins are bowled over, often played in English pubs.

clue.text: Team holding short reception in quarters

indicators.note: in means the shortened reception sits inside the pair of quarters

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass quarters

indicators.note: short means the word for the reception loses its final letter

parts.note: a levee is a formal reception, originally held by a monarch on rising

explanation.surface: A squad hosts a brief party in its lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings but means compass points E and N; LEVEE cut short is LEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in cricket or football fields this many players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Toothless old PM opening art gallery

indicators.note: opening means the old PM comes first, at the start of the gallery

parts.note: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister 1955-57
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A former prime minister without teeth opens an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' seems to be a ceremony but puts the PM first; Eden was Prime Minister in the 1950s and the Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate is a zoological term for lacking teeth, as anteaters and sloths do.
